summary.headline: Tilaknagar Q2 FY27 net revenue Rs 1,035 crore (+173% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 148 crore (14.3% margin), with inflation cutting margin about 2.5 points.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose sharply year-on-year on the Imperial Blue integration, but quarter-on-quarter volumes were flat (+2%) and NSR eased 0.75% to Rs 1,174 per case. Glass packaging and emerging ENA inflation pressured gross margin, which was 41.8% adjusted for subsidy versus 42.1% in Q1. Management maintained FY27 and FY29 guidance, citing Tamil Nadu regulatory reform, Karnataka recovery, and a price-mix lift of about 200 bps from future state price increases. Net debt eased slightly from June to Rs 2,074 crore.

segments.name: Imperial Blue Whisky
segments.commentary: Secondary volume grew 8.5% QoQ, with 100 bps Prestige & Above share gain. Karnataka volumes hit a record with share above 40%, up about 900 bps QoQ. Launched in Kerala in October 2026.

segments.name: Mansion House Brandy
segments.commentary: Secondary volume grew 7.1% QoQ, with 70 bps P&A share gain for TI. Mansion House Reserve in Tamil Nadu grew 25%+ QoQ and 50% YoY in September 2026. Named highest-selling brandy in Karnataka in September 2026.

segments.name: Samsara Gin (Spaceman Spirits Lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 50% in H1 FY27 over H1 FY26. About 35% of annual business falls in H1 and 65% in H2.

segments.name: Bodega Suprema No. 5 (tequila, Black Tiger Distilleries)
segments.commentary: TI invested Rs 22 crore for a 30% stake, with Rs 6 crore already invested and Rs 16 crore due within 12 months. Available in Maharashtra, with dispatch under way to Karnataka, Goa and Delhi.

guidance_outlook: FY27 combined-business volume growth guided at high single-digit to low double-digit; Imperial Blue expected to grow double digits in FY27.
Beyond FY27: mid-teens volume growth and mid-to-high teens revenue growth over the next couple of years.
Combined EBITDA margin target of 16%-18% by FY29 with upward bias; UK FTA benefit of about 100 bps on a full-year basis is included in the upper end of 18%.
Net debt to EBITDA below 1.0x by March 2029; net debt targeted below March 2026 levels by March 2027.
Integration exceptional costs of about Rs 10-11 crore per quarter over Q3 and Q4 FY27; no TSMA fees expected in FY28.
Margin expansion expected in H2 FY27 versus H1 FY26, assuming no large further inflation; YoY expansion expected from FY28.
capex_capacity: Bodega tequila investment: Rs 22 crore for 30% stake; Rs 6 crore invested, Rs 16 crore to follow within 12 months.
Integration of IB states that moved out of TSMA is stabilised; the last remaining state moves to TI operations towards end-FY27.
Luxury portfolio (Monarch Legacy, Seven Islands, Samsara) to roll out in northern states in Q3 and Q4 FY27 via Imperial Blue distribution.
Supply chain actions include higher bottle utilisation rates and packaging optimisation; no specific capacity figures given.
demand_pricing: Primary dispatches exceeded secondary in Q1 FY27 in exited TSMA states and planned-exit states, so Q2 volumes were flat QoQ.
Management says Imperial Blue run-rate in Q2 was close to the 2 million cases per month seen in May and June, with festival seasonality in North India.
Tamil Nadu: P&A brandy peaked at about 3 million cases; current run-rate is below 0.5 million cases per quarter.
Pricing: price increases taken in Assam, Meghalaya and underway in Arunachal Pradesh; talks ongoing with Telangana and Andhra Pradesh governments. Price-mix guidance of about 200 bps.
Competition: new entrants in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are concentrated in popular and below segments; TI says it is holding share at its price points.

qa_highlights.question: Could management confirm the Tamil Nadu reform numbers and size realistic volume potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Mansion House Reserve grew 25% QoQ and 50% YoY in September 2026. Management declined to forecast reform-driven volumes, but noted the peak of about 3 million cases versus under 0.5 million now.

qa_highlights.question: What was the working capital and receivables position versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross working capital days rose about 5 days versus March 2026, partly because IB was acquired on a zero-receivable, zero-payable basis. Annualised net working capital days are around 65, including about Rs 550 crore of Telangana overdues. Management expects similar levels excluding a potential recovery over 12-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much did raw-material inflation hit gross margin, and what subsidy income was there?
qa_highlights.answer: The inflation impact was about 2.5% of gross margin, or about Rs 25 crore per quarter in Q1 and Q2. Subsidy income was about Rs 20 crore in Q1 and about Rs 2 crore in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UK FTA benefit and when does it flow through?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps on a full-year consolidated basis is included in the 18% upper end of the margin guidance. There was no benefit in Q2 because the stock is still in inventory, and management declined to say when the benefit would start.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.5% margin headwind and FY27 margin expansion achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 FY27 margins to expand versus H1 FY26, assuming no large new inflation. Its FY28 launches at higher price points are expected to support year-on-year margin expansion.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from glass and ENA inflation; management expects ENA prices to stay elevated near term.
Possible UK FTA-related classification issue for scotch imports under HSN code; management is working with industry bodies and authorities, with no clarity yet.
Telangana receivables of about Rs 550 crore overdue on a six-month cycle, which keeps working capital days elevated.
Tamil Nadu reform timing and extent remain uncertain; management says it cannot predict regulatory outcomes.
Imperial Blue volume run-rate needs to pick up in H2 to meet double-digit FY27 growth; Q2 was seasonally soft.
Subsidy income is volatile (Rs 20 crore in Q1 versus Rs 2 crore in Q2) and is not guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on brand momentum, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and FY27 volume guidance. Noticeably cautious on near-term margins, with inflation and the timing of price increases left open. Evasive on UK FTA timing and on subsidy expectations.
key_quotes: Excluding the impact of inflationary pressures, the margin would have been higher, closer to 44%.
We maintain our guidance for FY27 of achieving a high single-digit to low double-digit volume growth for the combined business.
Our target is to take the net debt in March 2027 to below March 2026 levels.
We do not see any risk on that number.

Last remaining IB state moves to TI operations (integration, not new capacity)

growth.why: Management held FY27 combined volume growth guidance at high single-digit to low double-digit and mid-teens volume growth beyond FY27, backed mainly by share gains (IB Prestige & Above +100 bps, Karnataka share above 40%), ~200 bps price-mix from state price increases and northern luxury roll-out, with no specific new production capacity added.
